sources.entry: KeystoneJS - CMS and web application platform. (Source Code) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: KeystoneJS is a Node.js framework for building content management systems and web applications, generating a GraphQL API and admin UI from a schema you describe.
summary.what_it_does: Keystone lets you describe your data schema and generates a GraphQL API and a management UI for your content. The README says it aims to avoid boilerplate and bootstrapping while leaving room for custom back-end code. Keystone 6 packages are published to npm under the @keystone-6/* namespace. The README links to external documentation covering Why Keystone, a getting-started guide using the create-keystone-app CLI, examples, an API reference, and guides. Keystone follows semver. The Keystone 5 codebase is in maintenance mode in a separate repository.
use_cases: generating a GraphQL API from a data schema
creating an admin UI for content
back-end for a custom web application
prototyping a bespoke back-end without boilerplate
how_to_run: Use the create-keystone-app CLI to start a new project (per the Getting Started guide linked in the README)
notable: Schema-first: describe your data model and get a GraphQL API and management UI
Keystone 6 packages published under the @keystone-6 npm namespace
Official examples directory for running projects locally
caveats: Keystone 5 is in maintenance mode and lives in a separate repository
Targets Node.js Maintenance and Active LTS versions; Pending or End-of-Life Node versions may have problems
